note: Recorded baselines for the CI regression gate. Measured, not guessed.
The gate runs on the OFFLINE adapters, which are deterministic -- so a drop is a
real pipeline regression rather than model variance, and CI needs no API key.
The gate PINS its corpus (--corpus generated --count 40). It first inherited the
CLI default, and when that default changed from the 5-document seed corpus to the
40-document generated one, the recorded threshold silently stopped describing the
run it gated. A gate must name exactly what it measures.
It gates D-hybrid rather than B-dense because D exercises both retrieval arms and
the fusion between them, so it covers the most code. Checked retroactively: this
gate would have FAILED on the AND-semantics lexical bug (D scored 0.560 then,
against a floor of 0.858), which is the evidence it is set somewhere useful.

D-hybrid.gate_rationale: 3% below the recorded baseline, per docs/06 section 4.
D-hybrid.remeasured: 2026-09-19, after adding deterministic tiebreaks to both searches. Before that, equal scores came back in arbitrary order and D varied run to run (Gemini: 0.804/0.837/0.819 nDCG on identical inputs); now 0.572 offline, identical across runs. Floor unchanged at 0.56 (2% below).

gemini-retrieval-only.note: Gemini embeddings, varied phrasing. 87 texts embedded, 0 generation calls. D re-measured 2026-09-19 with deterministic tiebreaks.

offline_reference.note: All four arms, offline, generated-40, varied phrasing. Zero paid calls.
